Heard the learned counsel for the parties.

2. The appellant, owner of Hero Honda Splendor Motorcycle bearing registration No. BR-20E-6651 is in appeal against the award of compensation in T.M.V. Case No. 45 of 2003 whereby and whereunder liability to pay compensation has been fixed under section 166 of the M.V. Act upon the appellant.
3.

As per the claim application, deceased- Chand Mohammad Ansari, who was a pillion rider of JH 09B 6607 aged about 25 years died in a motor vehicle accident dashed with a motorcycle bearing registration No. BR 20E 6651.
As per the case of the claimants, the accident took place due to rash and negligent driving of motorcycle bearing registration No.BR-20E-6651 by the appellant.

sentences.text:
During inquiry before the Tribunal, a preliminary objection was raised on behalf of the appellant that at the relevant time of accident the appellant was driving motorcycle bearing registration No.
JH-09B-1750 which stood in the name of his brother- Om Prakash Sharma and the same was insured with the National Insurance Company.
The preliminary objection was allowed and the owner and insurer of motorcycle bearing registration no. JH-09B-1750 were also impleaded in the claim case.

5. The learned Tribunal framed the following main issues:
Issue No.iv:- whether the deceased (Chand Mohammad Ansari) died in motorcycle accident on 3.3.2003 at 7:30 a.m. near Vaibhav Hotel, Bye-Pass road, Chas, within jurisdiction of Chas P.S. due to rash and negligent driving of the motorcycle Hero Honda Splendor bearing registration no. BR-20E-6651 or by motorcycle bearing registration no. JH-09B-1750, which was driven by OP No.1 ?
Issue No.v:- whether the deceased died due to contributory negligence by the driver of LML Freedom motorcycle bearing registration no. JH-09B-6607 and by driver of Hero Honda Splendor motorcycle bearing registration no. BR- 20E-6651 or JH-09B-1750?

6. Learned Tribunal held that accident was caused by the rash and negligent driving of motor cycle bearing registration no.BR- 20E-6651 and directed the compensation be paid by the appellant who was driving the vehicle, as it was not under insurance cover at the time of the accident.
7. Heard both sides.

It is argued by the learned counsel on behalf of appellant that he was not the owner of the motorcycle bearing registration no.BR 20E 6651, yet the liability to pay the compensation has been fixed on him.
As matter of fact, he was not even driving the vehicle, as he was driving the motorcycle bearing registration no.JH 09B 1750 when it met with the accident.
It was for this reason that owner and insurer of JH 09B 1750, were impleaded as party.
Further, it was a case of head on collision between the two motorcycle as per the Tribunal's finding involving BR 20E 6651 and JH 09B 6607.
Despite evidence on record, A.W. 1- Sams Tabrej, the sole ocular witness who deposed that O.P. No.1/appellant was driving motorcycle bearing registration no.JH 09B 1750.
8. Learned counsel on behalf of respondents has defended the impugned order.
9. In motor accident claim cases, proof of fact is made by pre- ponderance of probability.
Considering the beneficial nature of legislation, procedural law does not rigidly apply in these cases.
This does not mean that the principles of appreciation of evidence has to be given a complete go bye.

The claimant brought a definite case that deceased died in a motor vehicle accident involving Hero Honda Motorcycle No.BR-20E-6651 when he was travelling as pillion rider on motorcycle number JH 09B 6607.
FIR (Exhibit 2) was lodged against the appellant stating him to be driving motorcycle no.BR 20E 6651 and the charge sheet (Exhibit 4) is also to the same effect.

Strangely enough,
applicant witness no.1- Sams Tabrej, who was driving motorcycle number JH 09B 6607 with the Bhagwat Prasad Sharma vs Razia Khatoon on 6 February, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/143872591/
2 deceased, has deposed that the offending motorcycle was JH 09B 1750.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Deposition of A.W. 3, who is another eye witness, also states that it was JH 09B 1750 which was the offending vehicle.
These evidences led on behalf of the claimant are beyond the pleading and in contradiction to the case set up by them.
Pleadings are the foundation of any civil case and the object that it should be supported by affidavit, is to ensure sanctity in the statement of facts asserted before the Court.
Affidavits are statement on oath and false affidavit can invite penal consequence.
O.P. witnesses have also stated that accident took place involving JH 09B 1750.
Except for the FIR and charge sheet, there is no other evidence to suggest that motorcycle no.BR 20E 6651 was involved in the accident.
For the present case either the pleading or the evidence on oath of the claimant is false.

10. Under the circumstance, the learned Tribunal has recorded a finding regarding involvement of motorcycle no. BR 20E 6651 in the accident as the offending vehicle is against the weight of evidence led on behalf of both the claimants as well as the opposite parties.

Finding is therefore,
unsustainable and is accordingly, set aside.
11. In view of the infirmities and contradictions in the claimant's case, the impugned order is set aside.
12. Miscellaneous Appeal is allowed.
Interlocutory Application, if any, is disposed of.
(GAUTAM KUMAR CHOUDHARY, J.)
